game:playstyle-desc-preset-roughseas: Standard survival on a world with open oceans, where wind, storms and the sea are dangerous.
game:worldattribute-dangerousOceans-desc: Storms, surf and the cold sea can break vessels and kill swimmers. Off, the sea keeps its weather but does no harm.
itemdesc-anchorwarp: Nine ropes spliced into 90 metres of warp. Stowed at a sailboat's mast, it lets the anchor reach deeper water.
item-handbooktext-reedboat:
A one-way crossing: quick to bind from reeds with a knife, light to carry, and it soaks up water and sinks within about three days afloat. It cannot be mended.
- Place it with a rightmouse click and paddle it with an oar.
- Pick it up with shift + rightmouse.
item-handbooktext-dugout-*:
One log hollowed out: the toughest hull before planks, barely scratched by rocks, and it needs no upkeep. Too heavy to carry; a workhorse of rivers and lakes.
- Place it with a rightmouse click where it will stay, and paddle it with an oar.
- Mend it with a log of its wood.
item-handbooktext-coracle:
A round bowl of hide for one. It spins on the spot and is poor in a straight line: for fishing and short crossings. It is light enough to wear on your back.
- Paddle it with an oar.
- Pick it up with shift + rightmouse, and put it in a backpack slot to carry it on your back.
- Mend it with leather.
item-handbooktext-barkcanoe:
Birch bark on a light frame: fast, with a draft so shallow that it runs rapids which batter every other hull. Fragile, and carried over portages.
- Paddle it with an oar.
- Pick it up with shift + rightmouse.
- Mend it on the way with birch bark.
item-handbooktext-currach:
Greased hide on a wooden frame: light, and it carries cargo along the coast under oars. Rocks hole the hide, and it wears unless greased with rendered fat every few days afloat.
- Paddle it with an oar.
- Pick it up with shift + rightmouse.
- Grease and mend it with rendered fat.
item-handbooktext-outrigger-*:
A narrow log hull steadied by a float: the fastest thing at sea before metal. Little cargo, clumsy in tight water, and too heavy to carry or beach.
- rightmouse click the halyard cleat at the mast to raise or lower the sail.
- Mend it with planks of its wood.
